title: fix(console): make `invalid_type` decisive in `refusesKind`, so union-typed members are judged by what the contract refused (objectui#8204)
body:
Fixes #8204

Test-only. One logic line added and one removed, both inside `refusesKind`; everything
else in the diff is prose and a changeset.

## What was actually wrong — the first suspected mechanism is FALSE

objectui#8204 suspected that `refusesKind` does not recurse into `z.union`. Measured on
disk: **it does.** The `invalid_union` arm at the bottom of the `every` runs, and it is
what carries branch verdicts up. The defect was one level in — in how a single branch's
issues were read.

`refusesKind` asked *"is EVERY complaint at this node a kind complaint"*. Zod keeps
running a schema's checks after its type check has already failed, so one node can carry
both kinds of complaint at once. For `z.string().min(1)` the probe `[]` comes back as
`invalid_type` (expected string) **and** `too_small` (`[].length` is 0). Read by `every`,
that pair is a CONTENT refusal — and the value it describes is an array the contract
refused for being an array.

The cleanest evidence is two probes on one key, differing only by the artefact issue.
`@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0 declares
`RecordActivityProps.types = z.array(z.union([FeedItemType, z.string().min(1)]))`:

```
probe []           branch 2 -> [invalid_type, too_small]  -> every() false -> refuses-content
probe ['Account']  branch 2 -> [invalid_type]             -> every() true  -> refuses-kind
```

Same key, same coarse kind, opposite verdicts. `[]` is the first array probe and the
accepted-kind walk is a `some`, so that one probe alone put `array` into the key's
accepted set.

## The fix

`invalid_type` at a node is now decisive, ahead of the `every`. This is a statement about
the contract, not about Zod: `invalid_type` says the value is not of that node's type, and
a value cannot be simultaneously the right kind and the wrong one, so whatever else the
node says about a value it has already refused for its kind is downstream of that refusal
rather than a second opinion competing with it. `too_small` on a non-string is exactly
such an artefact — "too short" is not a claim anyone would make about `[]` against a
string contract. The change also makes the `invalid_type` arm of the `every` unreachable,
so it is gone.

## The second suspected mechanism is INTENDED, and is now documented

`acceptedMemberKinds` counting a kind when the verdict is `accepts` **or**
`refuses-content` is deliberate, is the same fold `judgeMembers` and the arm direction
already make, and is load-bearing. Measured on 17.2.0, where `record:activity.types` is a
bare `z.enum([...])` of strings: every string probe is refused as `invalid_value`,
`'Account'` among them, so an `accepts`-only reading answers `{}` for a key whose
`of: 'string'` was derived from that very enum, and the one-kind assertion would red on a
declaration that is right. The fold was never the leak; it was the amplifier. A comment at
the helper now says so, as objectui#8204 asked.

## Measurements

Verdicts are `safeParse` against the **installed** `@objectstack/spec` artifact, and the
kind sets are the gate's own, from its own failure message.

**The CI list is not derived — three of its four names are clean.** CI on PR #7685 head
`f1e02a88f` named `element:record_picker.sort`, `object-grid.searchableFields` and
`page:accordion.items` alongside `record:activity.types`. They appear because that
assertion's message prints **every** judged row; the received array held exactly one
element. Measured on 17.3.0:

| member | accepted kinds, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `record:activity.types` | `{string,array}` | **`{string}`** |
| `element:record_picker.sort` | `{object}` | `{object}` |
| `object-grid.searchableFields` | `{string}` | `{string}` |
| `page:accordion.items` | `{object}` | `{object}` |

**Positive control — a genuine multi-kind member stays multi-kind.**
`record:highlights.fields` is a real member union (a field NAME or an inline field object)
and is the one key `MULTI_KIND_MEMBER_CONTRACTS` pins. It reads `{string,object}` before
**and** after, on 17.2.0 and on 17.3.0. So the fix did not collapse members to one kind.
Across all sixteen keys checked on both spec versions, **exactly one row moves**:
`record:activity.types` on 17.3.0.

**The gate itself, run against a real 17.3.0 artifact** (the installed 17.2.0 package
swapped for a registry copy of 17.3.0 under the repository's own zod 4.4.3, then restored
and the restore proven by sha256 of `dist/ui/index.mjs`):

```
before  Tests  7 failed | 174 passed (181)
after   Tests  6 failed | 175 passed (181)
```

The failure that disappears is `member declarations are derived from single-kind member
contracts` — this card's. **No new failure appears.**

**The remaining six are not this card's, and one of them is red on purpose.**
`the member judge reds on the drift that started this` fails at
`expect(specMemberVerdict('record:activity', 'types', 'array', 'Account')).toBe('refuses-content')`
— `accepts` received, because 17.3.0's open vocabulary genuinely accepts it. That is
failure (1) of objectui#8137, it sits on the manual floor, it is undecided, and it is
untouched here. The other five are 17.3.0 spec-drift ledger failures around
`object-grid.defaultSort`, which belong to objectui#7122 / PR #7685.

## Gates

All at `65b2e6451`; `git status` is empty at that commit, so every figure below was
measured on that tree.

- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` on the
  installed 17.2.0 — `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 181 passed (181)`, unchanged from
  the pre-fix baseline.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/` — `Test Files 89 passed (89)`, `Tests 1052 passed (1052)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console run lint` — 0 errors (208 pre-existing warnings, none
  in this file; `eslint --format json` on the changed file reports 0/0).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console run type-check` — exit 0, after
  `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build`. `tsc --listFiles` confirms the changed
  file is in the program, so the green is a measurement of it and not an `exclude`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — OK, empty-frontmatter declaration.
- `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` — OK.

## Coordination with objectui#8176

Per the file/region granularity ruling (maintainer, 2026-09-05), the regions touched are:

- `refusesKind` and its doc comment — the shared classifier in the **ARM direction**
  helper block (`objectui#4971`), lines ~1124-1180.
- One comment block above `acceptedMemberKinds` inside the **MEMBER direction**
  (`objectui#8067`) test `member declarations are derived from single-kind member contracts`,
  line ~2705.

objectui#8176 works the **REVERSE direction** (`objectui#3808`, eager-registration judging),
whose block begins at line 2189 and whose helpers sit above line 700. No overlap: nothing
in this diff falls inside the reverse-direction block, and no reverse-direction assertion
or helper is read or written here. There is no collision to merge around.

## Scope bans, honoured

- No `MULTI_KIND_MEMBER_CONTRACTS` entry added.
- No expectation literal, calibration control or `it(...)` assertion edited. The diff
  contains no `expect(`, `toBe(`, `toEqual(`, or probe-table line on either side.
- A green suite was not the criterion, and the suite is not green on 17.3.0. It should
  not be.
